name: User
rationale: The schema needs a base authenticated actor type for login/session-bound protected actions.
plain_english_summary: A person with an iTrust account who can authenticate to the system.
source_excerpt: ordinary authenticated User

name: User__mid
rationale: MID is used for authentication and is explicitly protected from patient edits.
plain_english_summary: The user's medical identification number used to identify the account.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.
alternatives_considered: Modeled as an entity identifier only; rejected because policies mention assigning and editing MID.

name: User__password
rationale: Password is a credential field whose visibility and assignment are access-controlled.
plain_english_summary: The secret password used by the user to log in.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.
alternatives_considered: Omit secrets from schema; rejected because credential secrecy rules must reference the field.

name: User__securityQuestion
rationale: Security question is explicitly named as information HCPs must not enter, edit, or view.
plain_english_summary: The account security question associated with a user.
source_excerpt: The HCP must not enter, edit, or view the patient's security question or password.
alternatives_considered: Represent as part of credentials record; rejected because only one credential field is repeatedly reused.

name: Patient
rationale: Patients are principals and resources with patient-specific records, account state, and designation relationships.
plain_english_summary: A patient in the medical-records system.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: Patient__active
rationale: Patient deactivation controls modification and login and administrator-only reactivation.
plain_english_summary: Whether the patient account is currently active.
source_excerpt: A deactivated patient cannot be modified or log into the system and can only be reactivated by an administrator.
alternatives_considered: Use a status enum; rejected because the spec only distinguishes deactivated versus active/reactivated.

name: HCP
rationale: Health-care professionals are principals for creating patients and editing patient records.
plain_english_summary: A health-care professional user.
source_excerpt: Doctors and other health-care workers can obtain and share essential patient information and view aggregate patient data.

name: LHCP
rationale: Licensed health-care professionals are principals and patient-designated providers with special viewing rights.
plain_english_summary: A licensed health-care professional.
source_excerpt: A LHCP is allowed by a particular patient to view approved medical records.

name: LHCP__hospitals
rationale: Administrators assign LHCPs to hospitals from a hospital list.
plain_english_summary: The hospitals to which a licensed health-care professional is assigned.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, choosing only hospitals from the hospital list.
alternatives_considered: Model assignment as a separate join entity; rejected because the spec only needs membership in multiple hospitals.

name: Administrator
rationale: Administrators create staff users, assign credentials, configure inactivity, and reactivate patients.
plain_english_summary: An administrative user of iTrust.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: EmergencyResponder
rationale: Emergency responders are listed as important actors and administrator-created users.
plain_english_summary: A user who responds to medical emergencies.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: UAP
rationale: Unlicensed personnel are created by LHCPs and can enter, edit, and view medical information.
plain_english_summary: An unlicensed assistive personnel user.
source_excerpt: A LHCP can create UAP users.

name: PersonalRepresentative
rationale: Personal representative status is a patient-specific relationship for viewing represented patients' information.
plain_english_summary: A user acting as a representative for a patient.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.

name: PublicHealthAgent
rationale: Public health agents are administrator-created actors in the healthcare slice.
plain_english_summary: A public health agent account.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: LabTechnician
rationale: Lab technicians are administrator-created actors in the healthcare slice.
plain_english_summary: A lab technician account.
source_excerpt: An administrator can create LHCPs, emergency responders, lab technicians, and public health agents.

name: SoftwareTester
rationale: Software tester is listed as an important actor type.
plain_english_summary: A software tester account.
source_excerpt: Important actors include Patient, HCP, LHCP, DLHCP, Administrator, Emergency Responder, UAP, Personal Representative, Public Health Agent, Lab Technician, Software Tester, and ordinary authenticated User.

name: Session
rationale: Protected actions depend on authenticated sessions and session expiration state.
plain_english_summary: A user's authenticated application session.
source_excerpt: Authenticated sessions terminate after inactivity, logout, or closing the application.

name: Session__user
rationale: The session must be tied to the active requester for session-bound authorization.
plain_english_summary: The user who owns the session.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.
alternatives_considered: Use principal only; rejected because session lifecycle must be modeled once and propagated.

name: Session__active
rationale: Authorization is disabled after session inactivity or termination.
plain_english_summary: Whether the session is currently active.
source_excerpt: After the inactivity limit is exceeded, authorization is disabled.
alternatives_considered: Represent only last activity timestamp; rejected because the policy needs a direct active/expired hook.

name: SystemSettings
rationale: Administrator-configurable inactivity period length is a global authorization-relevant setting.
plain_english_summary: System-wide administrative settings for iTrust.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: SystemSettings__inactivityPeriodLength
rationale: The inactivity period length is explicitly set by administrators.
plain_english_summary: How long a session may be inactive before authorization is disabled.
source_excerpt: The administrator can set the inactivity period length.

name: Hospital
rationale: LHCP assignment is constrained to hospitals from the hospital list.
plain_english_summary: A hospital in the approved hospital list.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign an LHCP to multiple hospitals, choosing only hospitals from the hospital list.

name: PatientAccount
rationale: Patient accounts are listed as important resources and are created, disabled, modified, and reactivated.
plain_english_summary: The account record for a patient.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patient accounts, credentials, demographic information, medical records, diagnostic information, office visits, access logs, provider designations, personal-representative relationships, and authenticated sessions.

name: PatientAccount__patient
rationale: Account actions are for a selected patient and need a link to that patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose account this is.
source_excerpt: An HCP can create or disable a selected patient.
alternatives_considered: Use Patient directly as the resource; retained PatientAccount to model account and credential resources separately.

name: Credentials
rationale: Credentials are important resources and are controlled separately from general patient data.
plain_english_summary: Login credential information such as MID and password.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patient accounts, credentials, demographic information, medical records, diagnostic information, office visits, access logs, provider designations, personal-representative relationships, and authenticated sessions.

name: Credentials__user
rationale: Credential records must be associated with the user whose MID/password they contain.
plain_english_summary: The user these credentials belong to.
source_excerpt: A user authenticates with MID and password.

name: Credentials__mid
rationale: MID is assigned to LHCPs and used for authentication.
plain_english_summary: The medical identification number stored in the credential record.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign medical identification numbers and passwords to LHCPs.

name: Credentials__password
rationale: Password is assigned to LHCPs and used for authentication.
plain_english_summary: The password stored in the credential record.
source_excerpt: An administrator can assign medical identification numbers and passwords to LHCPs.

name: DemographicInformation
rationale: Demographic information is a named resource entered and edited by UAPs.
plain_english_summary: Basic demographic data for a patient.
source_excerpt: UAP can enter and edit demographic information, diagnosis, office visit notes, and other medical information, and can view records.

name: DemographicInformation__patient
rationale: Demographic information belongs to a patient record.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose demographics these are.
source_excerpt: demographic information
alternatives_considered: Infer ownership through MedicalRecord; rejected because demographic information is named as its own resource.

name: MedicalRecord
rationale: Medical records are central protected resources viewable by patients, representatives, and LHCPs.
plain_english_summary: A patient's medical record.
source_excerpt: Important resources include patient accounts, credentials, demographic information, medical records, diagnostic information, office visits, access logs, provider designations, personal-representative relationships, and authenticated sessions.

name: MedicalRecord__patient
rationale: Own-record and represented-record access requires the medical record's patient owner.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose medical record this is.
source_excerpt: their own records and for patients they represent

name: DiagnosticInformation
rationale: Diagnostic information has patient-controlled viewing restrictions and approved-view semantics.
plain_english_summary: Diagnosis-related information in a patient's record.
source_excerpt: Approved diagnostic information is diagnostic information that a patient allows a designated or other licensed health-care professional to view.

name: DiagnosticInformation__patient
rationale: Diagnostic access restrictions are determined for a specific patient's information.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose diagnostic information this is.
source_excerpt: diagnostic information that a patient allows

name: DiagnosticInformation__restricted
rationale: The spec allows patients to restrict selected diagnostic information.
plain_english_summary: Whether this diagnosis has patient-controlled viewing restrictions.
source_excerpt: For selected diagnostic information, such as mental-illness, substance-abuse, or cosmetic surgery diagnoses, the patient can restrict viewing.
alternatives_considered: Use diagnosis category enum only; rejected because any selected diagnosis may be restricted.

name: DiagnosticInformation__restrictionAllowed
rationale: An LHCP determines whether a patient is allowed to restrict viewing of a diagnosis.
plain_english_summary: Whether the patient is allowed to restrict viewing of this diagnosis.
source_excerpt: A licensed health-care professional determines whether the patient is allowed to restrict viewing of a diagnosis.

name: DiagnosticInformation__viewAudience
rationale: Restricted diagnostic information can be visible to designated LHCPs, other LHCPs, or no one.
plain_english_summary: Who the patient has chosen may view restricted diagnostic information.
source_excerpt: A patient can enable designated licensed health-care professionals, other licensed health-care professionals, or no one to view restricted diagnostic information.
alternatives_considered: Use enum entity; rejected to avoid over-modeling three values in Stage 1.

name: OfficeVisit
rationale: Office visits are protected resources that HCPs document/edit and patients may view through their records.
plain_english_summary: A recorded medical office visit for a patient.
source_excerpt: An HCP can document and edit office visits for a selected patient, including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals.

name: OfficeVisit__patient
rationale: Office visits are for selected patients and support own/represented access checks.
plain_english_summary: The patient associated with this office visit.
source_excerpt: office visits for a selected patient

name: OfficeVisit__hospital
rationale: Hospital is included in documented office visits.
plain_english_summary: The hospital where the office visit occurred.
source_excerpt: including date, hospital, notes, prescriptions, lab procedures, diagnoses, procedures, immunizations, and referrals

name: OfficeVisit__surveyTaken
rationale: Survey access depends on whether the office-visit satisfaction survey has already been taken.
plain_english_summary: Whether a satisfaction survey has already been submitted for this office visit.
source_excerpt: If a patient or personal representative has not taken an office-visit satisfaction survey, they may take the survey; after the survey has been taken, they cannot take or view the previously submitted survey through that path.
alternatives_considered: Use a separate Survey entity; rejected because the rule hinges on a single taken/not-taken state.

name: AccessLog
rationale: Access logs are protected resources viewable by patients and representatives.
plain_english_summary: A log of access to a patient's information.
source_excerpt: A patient can view their own access log, or the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative.

name: AccessLog__patient
rationale: Access logs are patient-specific and representative access depends on the represented patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose access log this is.
source_excerpt: the access log for a person for whom they are a personal representative

name: AccessLog__accessorName
rationale: Access logs include the accessor name.
plain_english_summary: The name of the person who accessed the information.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__accessorRole
rationale: Access logs include the accessor role relative to the patient.
plain_english_summary: The accessor's role with respect to the patient.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__dateTime
rationale: Access logs include a date/time field.
plain_english_summary: When the access occurred.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: AccessLog__transactionType
rationale: Access logs include transaction type.
plain_english_summary: The type of access or transaction that occurred.
source_excerpt: Access logs include accessor name, accessor role relative to the patient, date/time, and transaction type.

name: ProviderDesignation
rationale: DLHCP is a patient-specific designation rather than a global role.
plain_english_summary: A record that a patient has designated a specific LHCP.
source_excerpt: A patient can designate or undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP for that patient.

name: ProviderDesignation__patient
rationale: The designation is for a particular patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient who made the designation.
source_excerpt: for that patient

name: ProviderDesignation__lhcp
rationale: The designation names the LHCP designated by the patient.
plain_english_summary: The licensed health-care professional designated by the patient.
source_excerpt: any LHCP as a DLHCP

name: ProviderDesignation__active
rationale: Undesignation requires representing whether the designation is currently active.
plain_english_summary: Whether the provider designation is currently in effect.
source_excerpt: designate or undesignate any LHCP as a DLHCP
alternatives_considered: Delete designation on undesignate; rejected because the patient can view LHCPs ever visited and designated.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship
rationale: Personal representative status is patient-specific and must be reusable across view actions.
plain_english_summary: A relationship showing that one user represents a particular patient.
source_excerpt: Personal representative status is also patient-specific.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship__patient
rationale: Representative access is for a represented patient.
plain_english_summary: The patient being represented.
source_excerpt: for patients they represent

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship__representative
rationale: The relationship must identify the representative user.
plain_english_summary: The user who is allowed to represent the patient.
source_excerpt: a person for whom they are a personal representative
alternatives_considered: Use PersonalRepresentative principal subtype only; rejected because the relation is patient-specific.

name: PersonalRepresentativeRelationship__active
rationale: Add/remove representative actions require current relationship state.
plain_english_summary: Whether the representation relationship currently applies.
source_excerpt: An HCP can add or remove another registered user as a personal health representative for a selected patient.

name: PersonalHealthInformation
rationale: Personal health information is a protected resource that HCPs edit and patients/representatives view.
plain_english_summary: Personal health information belonging to a patient.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: PersonalHealthInformation__patient
rationale: Own and represented access to personal health information requires the patient owner.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose personal health information this is.
source_excerpt: their own records and for patients they represent

name: FamilyHistory
rationale: Family history is a protected record component viewable by patients and representatives.
plain_english_summary: A patient's family medical history.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: FamilyHistory__patient
rationale: Family history access is for own or represented patient records.
plain_english_summary: The patient whose family history this is.
source_excerpt: their own records and for patients they represent

name: Immunization

plain_english_summary: A patient's immunization record item.
source_excerpt: A patient or personal representative can view medical records, family history, personal health information, immunizations, and office-visit information for their own records and for patients they represent.

name: Immunization__patient

plain_english_summary: The patient whose immunization this is.
